author: Hotochin
text:
Les_Paul wrote: this is how I see it so far:

I would be curious what IF or someone else has to say about your zones. I
 think you have it! Me and you seem to be similar. You made a comment in
 another post about overcomplicating things. I tend to do the same. I am
 very analytical and have to have everything laid out. Trading is not
always this way. I drew my zones the same way, but I found the opposing
FL differently. Let me explain.

In your diagram that I quoted above. Price is entering zone 3 from zone
2. I agree with how you found the upper FTR that formed the upper limit
of zone 3. The thing I am curious about is the lower limit of zone 3. I
see that in your drawing you waited for an engulf and FTR which created
the lower limit. You drew the limit from the origin of the engulf
though, not the FTR on the bottom. So the upper FL is from a FTR and the
 bottom is from the origin of an engulf. How I am thinking you find the
lower limits is by looking far the the left in the past to "predict"
where price will turn. In your scenario there is an engulf and FTR that
makes the lower zone. Make sense?

H

author: mettafort
text:
Hi Les_Paul and Hotochin,

I just wanted to add something which I dont think is always obvious.
When price breaks out and then retraces but holds under new demand that
has formed, out from the top of the PAZ, like the first example in the
chart LeS_Paul put togther, thats the failure-to-return - it tells us it
 couldnt return down because sitting here is fresh demand. When price
breaks out of PAZ 2, there is a clear RBR - the B is the FL, and then
price retraces, only for a bar. This bounces right above the FL - this
is the FTR as far as I understand it, because its major purpose for
being identified as a concept on the chart, is that it is a marker that
supply or demand is now imbalanced in the opposing direction - it is
another place that allows us to reason about order flow. And more
subtely, to me an FTR is the marker that price failed to get back to the
 origin of the move when it retraced, because of order flow.

I am sure you understand this actually, but thought maybe using some different verbiage might add to it.

MF.
